papers.title: Reducing Computational Complexity in CNNs: A Focus on VGG19 Pruning and Quantization
papers.subtitle: Published in International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications(ijacsa), Volume 16 Issue 6, 2025
papers.description: CNNs like VGG19 excel in computer vision but demand significant computational resources, hindering low-end device use. This study explores enhancing VGG19 efficiency via model compression: pruning (structured and unstructured) and quantization (8-bit and 4-bit QAT). Tested on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Oxford-IIIT Pet, methods reduced model size by up to 75% with lowered computational costs. 8-bit QAT notably compressed systems without sacrificing speed or accuracy. However, 4-bit QAT, despite 48% compression, reduced accuracy on complex datasets. Structured pruning sped up inference, and unstructured pruning improved accuracy, simplifying VGG19 for edge device implementation while maintaining prediction quality.

papers.title: Multi-Magnification Attention Fusion for Resource-Efficient Breast Cancer Classification with Integrated Grad-CAM Visualization
papers.subtitle: Unpublished paper
papers.description: This study develops a lightweight multi-magnification framework for clinical breast cancer classification, using depthwise separable convolutions and cross-magnification attention. Evaluated on BreakHis, it achieved 93.78% accuracy with 98% fewer parameters than traditional methods and 8.35ms inference time. The framework integrates interpretable Grad-CAM visualizations, enabling effective real-time screening in resource-constrained environments.
